235: Route Handlers will render a static response when running `next build`. Only the `GET` HTTP verb is supported. 323: ## Deploying
324: 
325: With a static export, Next.js can be deployed and hosted on any web server that can serve HTML/CSS/JS static assets.
326: 
327: When running `next build`, Next.js generates the static export into the `out` folder. For example, let's say you have the following routes:
328: 
329: - `/`
330: - `/blog/[id]`
331: 
332: After running `next build`, Next.js will generate the following files:
333: 
334: - `/out/index.html`
335: - `/out/404.html`
336: - `/out/blog/post-1.html`
337: - `/out/blog/post-2.html`
338: 
339: If you are using a static host like Nginx, you can configure rewrites from incoming requests to the correct files:
340: 
341: ```nginx filename="nginx.conf"
342: server {
343:   listen 80;
344:   server_name acme.com;
345: 
346:   root /var/www/out;
347: 
348:   location / {
349:       try_files $uri $uri.html $uri/ =404;
350:   }
351: 
352:   # This is necessary when `trailingSlash: false`.
353:   # You can omit this when `trailingSlash: true`.
354:   location /blog/ {
355:       rewrite ^/blog/(.*)$ /blog/$1.html break;
356:   }
357: 
358:   error_page 404 /404.html;
359:   location = /404.html {
360:       internal;
361:   }
362: }
363: ```
364:
